title: CDS English
summary: CDS English past questions, CDS 1 2017 to CDS 2 2026, five a day. Questions UPSC asked again and the question types it keeps asking come first, ranked together by how often they were asked, then every other question. A set of linked items counts as one question.
note: Repeats are counted across the 20 papers, CDS 1 2017 to CDS 2 2026. UPSC writes fresh sentences every paper, so repeats are few (a word, idiom or sentence that comes back) and most of the order comes from grammar-rule types. Groups were found by a chapter-by-chapter reading (scripts/homework/REVIEW_BRIEF_CDS_GAT.md) and checked in the main session.

groups.label: Proverb 'Where there is a will, there is a way'
'He succeeded by dint of perseverance and hard work'
'The information is available on the Internet'
Passive of the command 'Shut the door'
'Called on' meaning paid a visit to
Third conditional: 'If + had + past participle ... would have'
Conditional without 'if': 'Had he been ... would have'
Unreal present: 'If I were / I wish I were' ... 'would + verb'
Present tense (not 'will') in an 'if' or 'when' clause about the future
'Unless' means 'if not': choose the matching result
'A' or 'an' by the first sound (a unique, an honest, an MP)
'Each of' / 'either of' takes a singular verb
Nouns ending in -s that take a singular verb (news, politics)
'Whom' after a preposition (to whom, of whom)
'Has been + -ing' with 'since' for an action still going on
Word class of 'who' in a relative clause
Word class of a '-self' pronoun (himself, myself, thyself)
Word class of an exclamation (Alas, Hurrah, Oh no): interjection
Gerund, participle or infinitive: class of an -ing or 'to' verb form
'By' + means of travel or payment (by train, by bus, by card)
Preposition of time: in the morning, on Friday morning, at night
'Little / a little' with uncountable, 'few / a few' with countable nouns
'Whichever' for a choice from a set
Reported speech: tense moves back (will to would, has to had, now to then)
Indirect speech of a command: 'ordered ... to'
Indirect speech of a polite request: 'requested ... to'
Indirect speech of a question: 'asked' + if/wh-word, no inversion
Indirect speech: a universal truth keeps the present tense
Passive of a command: 'Let ... be ...' / 'should be ...'
Active to passive (and back) keeping the same tense
Meaning of 'at the drop of a hat'
Meaning of 'it's all Greek to me'
Order the passage on Britain, the first country to industrialise
'The' before a superlative (the largest, one of the most)
Uncountable nouns take no plural (furniture, equipment)
A singular determiner (a, an, every) needs a singular noun
Plural noun after few, most, two, hundreds of
Verbs that take no preposition (discuss, order, regret, consider)
'In' (not 'on') for inside a place or the body
'Who' or 'whom' in a question or relative clause
Pronoun agrees in number with its noun (every student ... his; animals ... their)
Redundant word repeating the verb's meaning (return back, circumnavigate around)
Subject joined by 'along with', 'with' or 'as well as': verb agrees with the first subject
'One of the ... who/that' takes a plural verb
Each, every, neither of: singular verb
Verb after 'there' agrees with the noun that follows
Verb agrees with the head noun, not the noun in the phrase after it
Either ... or / neither ... nor: verb agrees with the nearer subject
'If I were' in an unreal condition
Third conditional: 'If + had + past participle ... would have'
Stative verbs (own, exist, think = believe) not in the continuous
Reported speech: tense moves back (he had done, she would help)
Past and past participle of irregular verbs (swept, run, hung, sprang)
Passive voice form: be + past participle
Base form of the verb after a modal (can pursue, can succeed)
